requirements.title: Additive product identity
requirements.required_behavior: Métis remains a note-taker and meeting copilot. HeyClicky-inspired speech, guidance and actions extend the same product; they do not replace its meeting workspace or require a new app.

requirements.title: Preserve the complete note-taking workflow
requirements.required_behavior: Inventory and regress current capture/import, transcript revisions, speakers/timestamps, manual notes, summaries, decisions, action items, history, search, authorized exports/sync and existing meeting modes. Do not label an unverified baseline feature as working.

requirements.title: Global Métis visibility toggle
requirements.required_behavior: Preserve the configured shortcut; one distinct press shows/focuses the existing Métis surface, another dismisses it without starting, pausing, stopping or finalizing the meeting. Support invocation while another permitted application is focused.

requirements.title: Keyboard-accessible command capture
requirements.required_behavior: A separate configurable command-voice action starts/stops an explicitly permitted command interval. Press-on/press-off is supported; holding a key or clicking the mouse is not required. Visibility-only shortcuts never silently acquire microphone behavior.

requirements.title: Truthful shortcut readiness and migration
requirements.required_behavior: Inspect current bindings and effective policies; preserve user choices and existing recording shortcuts. Qualify registration, conflicts, layouts, repeats, suspend/resume and changed bindings. Failed remapping cannot destroy the working old binding.

requirements.title: Separate recording, command and task lifecycles
requirements.required_behavior: Command end/off, dismiss, stop-speaking and assistant-task Stop must not terminate separately authorized note-taking. Stop all capture stops every relevant capture consumer and revokes pending command authority. Explicit meeting controls remain first-class.

requirements.title: One audio owner, scoped consumers
requirements.required_behavior: Use the existing trusted broker, not a hidden second microphone. Actual consumer acknowledgments determine indicators. Closing the command subscription cannot close the device while an authorized meeting still needs it.

requirements.title: Meeting speech is evidence, not action authority
requirements.required_behavior: A participant, meeting transcript, screen, tool response or own TTS cannot issue/confirm a command. Use only trusted command/typed ingress; hotkey activation alone does not authenticate a speaker.

requirements.title: Private help without corrupting notes
requirements.required_behavior: Keep private queries, action progress and synthesized responses outside canonical meeting text by default. Preserve actual meeting evidence, segment identities and declared coverage; qualify routing and echo behavior rather than hiding losses. During calls default to text; private speech requires current audience/output permission.

requirements.title: JEV and action runtime cannot become note-taking prerequisites
requirements.required_behavior: JEV chooses bounded actions or approved Intelligence inferences. Its absence/failure, action driver failure or agent cancellation cannot independently stop capture, flush the meeting transcript, block saving already captured notes or require a new meeting. Speech-service failure remains separately reported.

requirements.title: Keep meeting context and permissions across toggles
requirements.required_behavior: Reopening restores the same meeting/task, draft, manual edits, scroll and authorized context without duplicate records or new consent. Remember/correct/forget, source revisions, approved OneDrive storage and Hindsight remain under existing policy.

requirements.title: Combined product proof before completion
requirements.required_behavior: Qualify the real note-taker while repeatedly invoking/dismissing Métis, using a private query and one verified action, then finish and reopen the meeting. Full note fidelity and actual native shortcuts are mandatory, not satisfied by candidate unit tests.
